title: 'Light My Fire' claims and being copied without a fee
summary: Gil describes a Columbia man urging him to sue over 'Light My Fire', and a film composer who used his record without paying.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: So I mean in cases like that you can institute a suit. It ~~es~~ takeSa long time. Somebody wanted me to do that for a tune I wrote that they said that the Doors ~~M~~ copied, 'Lite My Fire'. 'Lite My Fire' was such a big hit and sold to Buick and all that. So the man at Columbia was, caught on to it. I call him to try to place my album but he goes through a big thing about I should sue Elektra and the publisher and all that for 'Lite My Fire'. And I'm only trying to place my album now, I don't want to go through all that. He sent the lawyer over. He was so convinced that they had stolen it from me because he was employed at Prestige when I had made ~~that~~ This particular album and remembered my number. I didn't

even know what he was talking about. So after I went and got the record out and played it you know. And I saw what he meant. But I would never have thought of it. I mean things like that, I mean. So I mean you can't, I mean some people call it influence and people call it a tribute if you copy somebody. You know, somebody may copy copy somebody elses way of doing it, as a tribute. What they are doing is stealing it from them and calling it a tribute. All kinds of things like that. (LAUGHTER).
So I don't really have any stolen from me. I have never, I don't hold any, I have no rancor about anything like this. (I got the idea from ?).
Yes. I mean I thought, I told one guy one time that I thought it really wouldn't be too out of the way if he sent me a consultant's fee.

He told me what he did. He took my record and played it all the while they were making a movie. And then he went and wrote his own score based on that sound, you know, for the movie. So I said, gee, the least you could have done was sent me
a consultant's fee if you are going to use the record.
( ?) he wrote a song called 'The Shadow of your Smile'.
